scope: Dynamic solar time, atmospheric sky, moving sun/shadows and filtered sky illumination in the editor and runtime

units.note: Uses the existing documented large-fixture allowance; configured timeouts are unchanged. Five new daylight cases.

browser.command: npm run test:browser -- tests/browser/daylight.spec.mjs tests/browser/environment.spec.mjs tests/browser/settings-recovery.spec.mjs --output=.qa/daylight-final

coverage: Approximate solar position: east/west motion, latitude and seasons, north rotation, seamless midnight, polar day/night, finite direction and warm low-angle response.
Optional validated settings retain legacy static documents; JSON/native persistence; runtime ticks are independent of frame rate and do not mutate authored records.
Cached shadow bounds avoid rescanning terrain during playback; paused lighting stays fixed; leaving the dynamic sky disposes its resources and final disposal restores prior scene settings.
Rendered day/night difference, editable time, season and orientation, cycle speed and pause; advanced panels remain expanded across edits.
Playback leaves history and committed autosave unchanged while rendered time advances; GPU texture counts stay constant over several simulated hours in the fast-cycle fixture.
Native save, pause/undo/redo, autosave reload, embedded GLB round trip, standalone runtime restoration and rendered animation from a playing native document.

Four injected sky-capture/history failures, both during activation and active-sky replacement: exact viewport pixels, document, autosave and live texture counts survive. Failed activation retains redo. Retry and undo/redo succeed.
Importing EXR exits playback; enabling the sky retains embedded image bytes; invalid EXR replacements retain the dynamic sky; switching back to HDRI and fixed presets remains undoable.

visualReview.scene: Startup 192 m alpine terrain with 90 bundled photographic pine instances, wind disabled
visualReview.observations: Coherent bright daylight, warm sunset horizon, dim twilight and night silhouettes. Also inspected lower sky-intensity settings. Artist exposure/sky controls remain available.
visualReview.unrelatedConsoleMessage: favicon.ico returned 404; no shader/WebGL or uncaught page errors in this review.

fixesDuringVerification: Preserved expanded Light panels and scroll position after setting changes.
Fixed malformed season and lighting-preset option markup discovered by browser interaction.
Limited ground-bounce blending to the illumination probe so the visible sky remains continuous at the horizon.
limits: Chrome on Windows only. Cross-browser/mobile/device validation and dense realistic scene frame-time budgets remain open.
The procedural test fixture is small; the separate photographic-pine review validates rendering, not close-up foliage quality or AA production readiness.
Solar time uses a fixed season and approximate declination, without civil timezone, longitude, leap-year or atmospheric-refraction corrections.
Art-directed relative intensity, not measured irradiance or a calibrated physical daylight simulation. No volumetric clouds/fog, cloud shadows, moon or star field.

Filtered illumination uses a 128-pixel cube probe and two reusable PMREM outputs, refreshed at most twice per second. Fast cycles can expose this cadence; moving shadows remain limited by terrain extent and shadow-map settings.
Generic GLB viewers do not run the cycle; the toolkit restores it from embedded authoring data.
